- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates the drop; adjust downward by 2–5% relative to recent low.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2 days above peak, then allow gradual mean reversion.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (or vice versa), model lags by 1–3 days; adjust forecast to align with sentiment change 1–2 days ahead.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., price drops sharply after a peak), model often holds upward bias; apply downward correction by 3–8% of recent range.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to overfit recent trends; use 10–15% smoothing or apply moving average filter to dampen noise.
